name: Othine freckle remover

lead: Othine was a freckle remover advertised in the 1920s as a cream applied nightly to fade freckles, for a more even complexion. Historical overviews list it with Stillman's Freckle Cream and Berry's Freckle Ointment among commercial freckle removers that contained mercury compounds.

A 1928 advertisement shows it was also sold in a triple-strength version. A product called Othine Skin Bleach is sold today with hydroquinone as an active ingredient, which is a different formulation.

paras: Historically such creams were applied at night to freckled areas over weeks.
Mercury compounds in skin products are the subject of FDA warnings, and US regulation of them in cosmetics began in the 1940s with limits of 5 percent or less.

angle.text: The product was sold to fade freckles and leave a clearer-looking complexion.

lead: Othine Freckle Remover was a commercial freckle cream advertised in 1928, including in a triple-strength version.[1] Historical overviews list it among freckle removers that contained mercury compounds, typically combined with bismuth or zinc salts.[1]

Mercury freckle creams were common into the twentieth century; the US Food, Drugs and Cosmetics Act arrived in 1938, the FDA moved in the 1940s to limit mercury compounds to 5 percent or less, and the UK, US and EU restricted cosmetic mercury in the 1970s.[1]
infobox: Mercury compounds, as reported for such creams[1]

paras: The product appears with Stillman's and Berry's among widely used freckle removers.[1] Mercury creams of this type reached 10 to 15 percent mercury or more in some cases, and regulatory limits followed in the 1940s.[1]
